conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect a lower target return, around 1.5% per month, with significantly reduced risk and drawdowns. This is a defensive posture.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to 3% and 2% respectively.
Reduce other leveraged positions (METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU) to 3% or less.
Add AMZN at 5% as a new, high-quality long setup.
This balances risk reduction with selective growth opportunities.
Concentration is reduced while maintaining exposure to quality names.
Aims for steady growth with controlled risk.
balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a strong new name. Expect moderate returns with controlled drawdowns.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to 6% each.
Increase other leveraged positions (METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU) to 6% each.
Add NBIS at 9% as a top-rated scanner setup.
This plan aggressively leans into leverage and concentration.
It aims for maximum growth by pressing working sectors.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretched growth, aiming for around 4% per month. It increases leverage and concentration, including adding a new high-conviction name (NBIS). Be aware that this significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk, with leveraged ETFs experiencing daily decay.

plan: Sell all high-risk positions including SOXL, SPAL, CRWD, SMH, QQQ, and SPY.

This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions over growth.

income.read: This income-focused plan aims for steady monthly distributions, targeting around 1% per month. It eliminates growth-oriented and leveraged assets, shifting entirely to income-generating ETFs like QQQI. While prioritizing low drawdowns, NAV can still fall in market downturns.
